what_taken: Commentary arguing Australia should adopt an integrated population policy (pp. 12, 19). Permanent visa numbers are the main policy lever (p. 14). Dispersal of immigrant settlement away from Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane is a priority, as growth in the largest cities is the harder problem (p. 16). Fertility policy should aim at family wellbeing, not birth rates (pp. 17-18). A funded population research program is proposed (p. 18).

what_taken: Decomposes the rise in employed persons from July 2011 to July 2016 (738,800, or 6.8 per cent) on ABS data: net migration 613,400, population growth 98,900, participation change 26,500 (pp. 3, 8). Most migrant workers added were under 55 (595,300). Background traces the shift to skilled migration from 1995 (pp. 5-6). It measures employment, not population growth, and ends by urging infrastructure planning for growth (p. 11).

what_taken: Case study of 102 food-related policy documents (Queensland, Western Australia, Victoria, federal; collected July 2021 to October 2022), 25 policymaker interviews (2022) and 500 public surveys, all in Brisbane (2021) (p. 963). what_taken: Interviews with 25 senior planners and policymakers (QLD 15, WA 6, VIC 4; September to December 2022) (p. 532). Twenty-one (84 per cent) agree food is a stranger to urban planning (p. 534). Few food elements are integrated, primarily rural agricultural land protection and urban food retail; other food activities are incidental (pp. 536-537). Market pressures, land shortages and stakeholder conflicts limit new integration (p. 542).

what_taken: Tests whether the 2017 to 2019 Murray-Darling Basin drought was beyond natural variability, using linear inverse models trained on 1900-2016 rainfall and sea surface temperature (PDF pp. 1, 3). Cool-season and annual deficits, taken as a three-year basin-wide total, were unprecedented in the instrumental record and beyond the model range, most in the northern basin; single years mostly fell within the model range (PDF p. 6).
